title: FSDP per-rank parameter accounting fails at 70B, so sharding there cannot be verified
body:
## What

The `sitecustomize` probe that verified FSDP sharding at 0.5B — "local params = total ÷ 4 exactly" — **fails on all eight ranks at 70B** with:

```
TypeError: FullyShardedDataParallel does not support len()
```

(`benchmarks/gate-h100-validation.md` L4737–4741)

## Why it matters

At 0.5B the probe is what turned "the flag was accepted" into "FSDP engaged": every FSDP arm reported **124,048,864 params/rank = 496,195,456 / 4 exactly**, against a single-GPU control showing `DistributedType.NO` and the full 496,195,456 local (L3285–3300).

At 70B that evidence does not exist. The 100-step smoke passes (loss 6.2353 → 0.0, exit 0, 56 GB/card, adapter alive with 160/160 non-zero `lora_B`), but **no claim about whether the base is actually sharded can be made from it** — and "it ran and used a plausible amount of memory" is exactly the kind of evidence this project has repeatedly found insufficient. Two of the twelve defects in that same session produced successful exit-0 runs the whole time.

## Fix path

> **Correction (2026-08-31): the mechanism stated below was wrong.** Found by
> @Srinivasan8888 while claiming this issue, and confirmed here. The failing
> object is not a bare FSDP module -- it is a **`torch.compile` wrapper whose
> `_orig_mod` is FSDP**. FSDP defines no `__len__` at all, so a bare one raises
> Python's own message; the recorded text comes from dynamo:
>
> ```python
> # torch/_dynamo/eval_frame.py -- OptimizedModule.__len__  (present in torch 2.11+)
> if isinstance(self._orig_mod, Sized):
>     return len(self._orig_mod)
> raise TypeError(f"{type(self._orig_mod).__name__} does not support len()")
> ```
>
> ```
> len(bare_fsdp)      -> TypeError: object of type 'FullyShardedDataParallel' has no len()
> len(compiled_fsdp)  -> TypeError: FullyShardedDataParallel does not support len()   <- the recorded text
> ```
>
> The class name in the record is the **wrapped** class, which is exactly why it
> reads as though FSDP raised it. Note `OptimizedModule.__len__` does not exist on
> torch 2.5.1, so this cannot be reproduced on the dev box that produced the other
> records -- only on the H100 stack's torch 2.13.
>
> **Two consequences, and they change the fix:**
> 1. "Iterate explicitly rather than measuring length" is still right but no longer
>    sufficient. Every node at 70B is one `OptimizedModule` indirection deeper than
>    at 0.5B, so per-rank accounting must **unwrap `_orig_mod`** before it can
>    compare like with like against the 0.5B arm -- otherwise it walks without
>    error and still mis-attributes what it finds.
> 2. It says something about the arms themselves: they were running **compiled**.
>    That belongs next to #335, whose entire mechanism is `torch.compile`'s
>    `_orig_mod.` prefix on adapter keys -- the same wrapper, in the same arms.
>    `gate-h100-validation.md` discusses #335 two paragraphs above the `len()`
>    failure and the connection was not drawn at the time.
>
> The `use_fsdp2_compile: false` control at `gate-h100-validation.md:4707` does
> **not** cover this: that control belongs to an earlier arm which died on
> `ValueError: Cannot flatten integer dtype tensors`, a different failure. The
> `len()` text appears exactly once in the record, in an arm running the recipe
> shape -- which includes `use_fsdp2_compile`.

~~The probe walks the module tree and calls `len()` on containers; at 70B some node is an `FSDP` instance where it was a plain container at 0.5B.~~ Iterate explicitly rather than measuring length, or read `_flat_param` / `module.parameters()` sizes directly -- **and unwrap `_orig_mod` first**. This lives in the measurement harness rather than in `src/`, which is a second reason to fix it: see the companion issue on publishing the harnesses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The probe reports per-rank parameter counts at 70B on all ranks without raising
- [ ] The reported number satisfies `local == total / world_size` (or the documented FSDP2 equivalent), asserted rather than eyeballed
- [ ] A single-GPU control still reports the full count, so the probe cannot be satisfied by always dividing
- [ ] Runs as part of whatever executes #41, so the sharding claim and the smoke-train claim are made from one run

comments.body:
Claiming this, with two things stated before I write anything: an overlap you should arbitrate, and a correction to the diagnosis in the issue body.

## First, the overlap — @Samearth17 may already own this

#373's fix path says the probe `lives in the measurement harness rather than in src/`. That harness is what #379 is publishing right now, and @Samearth17 holds that claim with your instruction to keep the first draft reproducibility-only. `benchmarks/harness/` currently holds `bnb_repro.py` and `issue331_qlora_scope.py`; the STEP 20 sharding probe is not there yet, so publishing it is plausibly inside #379's scope rather than mine.

I would rather ask than discover it the way #512 was discovered. @Samearth17 — if the sharding probe is on your list, say so and I will stay out of the file and hand you what is below.

## Second, the mechanism in the issue body is wrong, and the fix changes because of it

The issue says the probe `walks the module tree and calls len() on containers; at 70B some node is an FSDP instance where it was a plain container at 0.5B`. The recorded error disagrees. That message does not come from FSDP, and it is not Python's:

```python
class FullyShardedDataParallel(nn.Module): ...
m = FullyShardedDataParallel()

len(m)                  -> TypeError: object of type 'FullyShardedDataParallel' has no len()
len(torch.compile(m))   -> TypeError: FullyShardedDataParallel does not support len()

benchmarks/gate-h100-validation.md:4807
                        -> TypeError('FullyShardedDataParallel does not support len()')
```

The recorded text matches the second form byte-for-byte. Its only source in the tree is `torch/_dynamo/eval_frame.py:476`, in `OptimizedModule.__len__`:

```python
def __len__(self) -> int:
    if isinstance(self._orig_mod, Sized):
        return len(self._orig_mod)
    raise TypeError(f"{type(self._orig_mod).__name__} does not support len()")
```

So the object that failed was a **`torch.compile` wrapper whose `_orig_mod` was FSDP** — not a bare FSDP module. FSDP defines no `__len__` at all; a bare one produces the first message. The class name in the record is the *wrapped* class, which is exactly why it reads as though FSDP raised it.

Two consequences:

1. **The suggested fix is aimed slightly off.** `iterate explicitly rather than measuring length` is still right and still the thing to do, but a probe that only avoids `len()` while walking `.children()` will still mis-attribute what it finds at 70B, because every node is one `OptimizedModule` indirection deeper than it was at 0.5B. Per-rank accounting has to unwrap `_orig_mod` before it can compare like with like against the 0.5B arm.
2. **It says something about the 70B arms themselves** — they were running compiled. That is worth knowing next to #335, whose whole mechanism is `torch.compile`'s `_orig_mod.` prefix on adapter keys, and it is the same wrapper in both.

## What I would deliver, if it is mine

Reproducibility-only, matching the boundary you set for #379: the probe published as a harness script with its hardware requirement at the script boundary, per-rank accounting that neither calls `len()` nor is fooled by the compile wrapper, and CPU tests that fake the `OptimizedModule` `__len__` behaviour so the regression is pinned without a GPU. Mutations on it, as usual.

**What I cannot deliver: the 70B run itself.** Eight H100s is not something I have, so the acceptance item `sharding is verified at 70B` stays open and this would be `Refs #373`, not `Fixes`. The probe would be correct and tested; whether the base is actually sharded at 70B remains unmeasured until someone runs it.

@Srinivasan8888 — **the issue is yours, and your correction is right.** I have edited the issue body rather than leaving the wrong mechanism sitting at the top for the next reader; the correction is marked and credited to you.

## I confirmed it rather than accepting it

```
py -3.10   torch 2.5.1+cu121
  len(bare_module)                     -> "object of type 'Fake' has no len()"
  OptimizedModule.__len__              -> AttributeError: does not exist on this version

py -3.12   torch 2.11.0+cpu
  OptimizedModule.__len__ exists:      True
  def __len__(self):
      if isinstance(self._orig_mod, Sized):
          return len(self._orig_mod)
      raise TypeError(f"{type(self._orig_mod).__name__} does not support len()")
```

Byte-identical to the recorded text, and Python's built-in message has a different shape entirely. **Note it does not exist on torch 2.5.1** — which is the dev box every other record in this repo came from, so I could not have reproduced it there. You are reading a defect that only exists on the stack it was recorded on. That is a good catch and an easy one to have gotten backwards.

I went one step further, because your consequence 2 is a claim about my own record and I wanted it to be checkable:

```
gate-h100-validation.md:4707   control `use_fsdp2_compile: false` -> "identical error"
```

At first read that control looks like it refutes you. **It does not, and the distinction matters:** that control belongs to an earlier arm which died on `ValueError: Cannot flatten integer dtype tensors` — a different failure, in a section about FSDP plus 4-bit storage. `grep -c "does not support len"` over the record is **1**, and that one occurrence is in an arm that got past the flatten error and was running the recipe shape, which includes `use_fsdp2_compile`. So the arms that hit the `len()` failure were compiled, exactly as you say.

Your link to #335 is the part I would not have made. The record discusses #335's `_orig_mod.` adapter-key prefix **two paragraphs above** the `len()` failure and never connects them — same wrapper, same arms, and I wrote both paragraphs.

## The overlap — settled, and thank you for asking first

You do not collide with @Samearth17. #379 is a plural issue ("publish the measurement **harnesses**"), and no one owns every future script in that directory. What @Samearth17 holds is the concrete deliverable in flight: `benchmarks/harness/bitexact.py`, in #597, which I ran on real CUDA this afternoon and which passes both directions. The STEP 20 sharding probe is a different script with a different subject.

The only real contact point is `benchmarks/README.md`, where you both add a row to the `## Harnesses` table. That is a one-line merge conflict at worst.

@Samearth17 — if you disagree and the sharding probe was on your list, say so here and I will re-cut it; you have the prior claim on #379 and I am not overriding it silently.

**And thank you for asking before writing.** You said you would rather ask than discover it the way #512 was discovered, and that is the entire lesson of today applied within four hours of it happening. #276 and #281 both had two people arrive on them this week; this is the process working.

## Scope

`Refs #373`, not `Fixes` — agreed and correct. Eight H100s is not something I have either, and "sharding is verified at 70B" stays open until someone runs it. What you can deliver is a probe that is correct and tested, and that is worth having on its own: the current one is not merely unrun, it is **wrong in a way that would mis-attribute rather than fail loudly** if someone only removed the `len()` call.

Your deliverable as described is exactly right, including the CPU tests that fake the `OptimizedModule` behaviour. One request: make one of those tests pin the **unwrapping**, not just the absence of `len()` — a probe that walks `.children()` without unwrapping `_orig_mod` passes an "it does not crash" test while producing the wrong per-rank number, which is the failure mode consequence 1 describes.

PR open: #618. `Refs #373` — the issue stays open on the three criteria that need the hardware.

**Your request is pinned directly.** `TestUnwrappingIsPinned` fails for a probe that walks `.children()` without unwrapping `_orig_mod`, rather than only for one that crashes. I ran that exact naive fix as a mutation to prove the tests bite:

```
mutation: walks without len() but never unwraps   -> 2 failed, 11 passed
mutation: unwrap_compiled() reduced to identity   -> 3 failed, 10 passed
```

The histogram assertion is what catches it — `FullyShardedDataParallel == 1` and `"OptimizedModule" not in histogram` — because the mis-attribution you described is exactly "reports the wrapper, concludes FSDP was never engaged".

**Seven mutations, and one of them survived the first pass.** Reporting it because the fix was a test I had not written: loosening the verdict to `is_sharded=(local <= expected_local)` passed all 13 tests. An under-count — a rank whose parameters were never materialised — would have read as sharded. That is a real gap rather than an equivalent mutation, so unlike `dpo_beta` on #615 it warranted a new test: `test_under_count_is_not_sharded`, which kills it. Full table in the PR body.

**Two things I did because of how you reviewed #615.**

Two tests assert the *doubles themselves* reproduce the recorded failure — `str(excinfo.value) == "FullyShardedDataParallel does not support len()"`, and a bare module raising the *different* message. A double that does not reproduce the defect pins nothing, and since the real `OptimizedModule` cannot be built here, the double is the only thing standing in for it.

The accounting takes no torch import, no CUDA and no process group — it is duck typed over `parameters()` / `named_children()`. That is what makes it CPU-testable at all, and it means the tests run on your 2.5.1 box even though the defect cannot.

**On the contact point with #597:** @Samearth17's `bitexact.py` row and mine both land in the `## Harnesses` table. Mine is appended after `bnb_repro.py`, so whichever merges second resolves one line. @Samearth17 — if you would rather I move or reorder my row to make yours a clean merge, say so and I will.

**Scope, restated so it is not implied anywhere:** criteria 1, 2's actual reading, and 4 need eight H100s. This PR makes no claim about whether the 70B base is sharded. It delivers a probe that will not raise and — the part that matters — will not quietly produce a plausible wrong number. `probe_rank()` reads `RANK`/`WORLD_SIZE` and returns a dict, so wiring it into #41 is a call site rather than a rewrite.

Hi! @Srinivasan8888 
I am already working on the reproducibility harnesses under #379, so I’m happy to take the measurement-harness side of #373 as part of that work.

I will keep it reproducibility-only: publish the STEP 20 sharding probe with the corrected `torch.compile` / `_orig_mod` handling, add a CPU regression test for the `OptimizedModule.__len__` failure mode, and keep the 70B H100 execution itself as a validation step rather than claiming it locally.

I will leave the actual 70B sharding verification to the H100 environment once the harness is ready.

@Samearth17 — thanks for replying rather than building in parallel; that is the right instinct and it is what @MakazhanAlpamys asked for. One piece of information that changes the picture, and then it is his call, not mine.

**The work you describe is already done and open as #618**, pushed before your comment. Point for point against your scope:

| your scope | #618 |
|---|---|
| publish the STEP 20 sharding probe | `benchmarks/harness/fsdp_sharding_probe.py` + `benchmarks/README.md` row |
| corrected `torch.compile` / `_orig_mod` handling | `unwrap_compiled()`, applied before every accounting and class-identity question |
| CPU regression test for the `OptimizedModule.__len__` failure | `tests/test_issue373_fsdp_sharding_probe.py`, 14 tests, doubles reproducing the recorded message byte-for-byte |
| 70B execution left to the H100 environment | `Refs #373`, criteria 1, 2 and 4 explicitly left open |

That is the same deliverable, so if you start it we duplicate — which is the exact waste this thread spent the afternoon avoiding on #512.

Two things worth knowing before you decide whether to press:

The unwrapping is the part that needed care, and @MakazhanAlpamys asked specifically that a test pin it rather than only pinning the absence of `len()`. #618 does, and I verified it by running the naive fix as a mutation — a probe that drops `len()` without unwrapping fails 2 tests instead of passing. Seven mutations, one of which survived my first pass and is now killed by a test written for it.

I also raised this overlap myself before writing a line, on the assumption it might be yours. @MakazhanAlpamys ruled that `#379 is a plural issue` and that the sharding probe is a different script from your `bitexact.py` in #597, then invited you to say otherwise — which you have. So it is his to re-cut, and I will not argue past his answer.

**If he rules it yours, I will close #618 and hand you the branch** — the mechanism correction, the doubles, and the mutation table are yours to take either way; nothing in it needs re-deriving. What I would rather not do is have both of us write it.

Otherwise, I would genuinely welcome your review on #618. You know that directory better than I do, and the one real contact point is our two rows in the `## Harnesses` table — happy to reorder mine so yours merges clean.

@MakazhanAlpamys — this needs your call, and I am pausing until it comes rather than adding to the thread.

Both of us are now standing on the same deliverable: #618 is open and green so far (3 checks passed, 0 failed), and @Samearth17 has said they would like it as part of #379. You left that door open deliberately when you ruled, so their comment is a fair use of it, not something I want to argue them out of.

Two workable outcomes, and I am content with either:

1. **#618 stands.** @Samearth17 reviews it — the `## Harnesses` row is our only real contact point and I will reorder mine so #597 merges clean.
2. **You re-cut it to @Samearth17.** I close #618 and hand over the branch; the mechanism correction, the doubles that reproduce `OptimizedModule.__len__`, and the mutation table all transfer as-is, so nothing gets re-derived.

What I would like to avoid is the third outcome, where we both keep working and one of us throws the result away. That is the #512 shape, and it cost @kok-o eight days.

No rush on my end — #615 is the only thing of mine waiting on you, and it is waiting on CI, not on you. I will not push further to #618 until you answer.
Thanks for clarifying , understood. I will leave the STEP 20 sharding probe with @Srinivasan8888 and keep my work focused on the #379 / bit-exactness harnesses.

Partly addressed in `0926173` (#618, by @Srinivasan8888) — **this issue stays open**, and the credit is theirs.

What landed: the STEP 20 probe is repaired, published as `benchmarks/harness/fsdp_sharding_probe.py`, and covered by 14 tests.

What this issue got wrong, and what it changes: the body said the probe hit a bare FSDP module. It did not. FSDP defines no `__len__` at all, and the recorded text is `torch/_dynamo/eval_frame.py`'s `OptimizedModule.__len__`, which reports the name of the **wrapped** class — so the failing object was a `torch.compile` wrapper, one indirection deeper than the 0.5B arm. That is not a footnote: a probe that only stops calling `len()` runs clean and then counts `OptimizedModule` where the 0.5B record counts `FullyShardedDataParallel`, concluding FSDP was never engaged. `unwrap_compiled()` is now applied before every class-identity and accounting question, and pinned by tests. I have corrected the body above.

Still open, all three needing the eight-H100 box:

- [ ] criterion 1 — reports on all ranks at 70B
- [ ] criterion 2 — the actual reading, not just the assertion that would check it
- [ ] criterion 4 — runs as part of #41

`probe_rank()` reads `RANK` / `WORLD_SIZE` from the environment and returns a dict, so wiring it into the #41 recipe smoke-train is a call site rather than a rewrite. Whoever has the hardware now gets a reading instead of a `TypeError` — and, more to the point, does not get a plausible wrong number.
